content.text: The check is `forbidAddedLinesMatching`, blocking after 2026-10-04 — so this bites every future rename, not just mine. Filing it.

input.title: no-new-long-dashes reads a pure rename as added lines, so moving a file with long dashes fires once per line
input.body:
`no-new-long-dashes` (`.claudinite/local/packs/claudinite/declared-checks.json`, `forbidAddedLinesMatching`, `since: 2026-09-20`) cannot see a rename: git reports a moved file as a whole-file addition unless rename detection is on, so every line of the moved file counts as added.

**Observed:** #2192 moves 36 `VERSIONS.md` files under `provenance/` with `git mv` and changes one line of content. The work sweep reports **196** findings, one per pre-existing long dash in the moved rows — text the `pack-version-history` task generated and that no one is adding now.

The check's own fix text already anticipates the case and cannot act on it: *"a line the change merely moved keeps its text, so re-add it as it was."* That is exactly right and exactly what the moved file does — the lines are byte-identical on both sides of the rename.

**Why it matters beyond this PR:** the grace ends **2026-10-04**, after which the rule blocks. From then, any change relocating a file that contains a long dash is blocked with one finding per line, and the only ways through are rewriting content the change never touched, or an `accept` waiver per line. Relocations are routine here — #2101 split three website packs, #1081 collapsed and renamed four, and the provenance work is still moving files.

**Shape of a fix** (engine work in the declared-check vocabulary, not a one-liner, which is why this is its own issue): have the work context read its diff with rename detection (`git diff -M` / `--find-renames`) and treat a renamed file's unchanged lines as unchanged rather than added, so only lines the change actually wrote reach `forbidAddedLinesMatching`. That serves every added-line check, not just this one. A narrower alternative — excluding a file whose pre-image is identical — buys the same result for pure moves only, and leaves a move-plus-edit still reporting the whole file.

Until it is fixed, a relocation after 2026-10-04 needs the finding waived deliberately rather than the moved text rewritten.
